**The deadly triad combines three individually useful ideas that can interact unstably.** Function approximation generalizes values across states. Bootstrapping uses estimated future values as targets. Off-policy learning updates from data generated by another policy. Together, estimation errors can feed back and grow rather than converge. [1](https://incompleteideas.net/book/the-book-2nd.html)

**The moving-target intuition.** A network predicts a value, uses a related network prediction to form its target, then changes weights shared across many states. That update alters both current predictions and future targets. Off-policy data can emphasize states/actions differently from the policy being evaluated, worsening the feedback.

Experience replay stores transitions and samples them in mixed order, reducing temporal correlation and improving reuse. A target network changes more slowly, making bootstrap targets less volatile while the online network learns. These were important stabilizers in DQN.

**Neither is a universal convergence proof.** Replay can contain stale or distributionally unsuitable data, and a frozen target can still be wrong. Update frequency, reward scale, exploration, architecture, and optimizer settings matter. Related improvements address overestimation or distribution shifts but do not erase every triad risk.

Track Q-value scale, actual returns, TD-error distribution, and performance across seeds. A falling replay loss can coexist with a poor policy because it measures fit to the current targets, which may themselves be inaccurate or unstable.

**Technical details and references.**

The deadly triad combines function approximation, bootstrapped targets, and learning from a behavior distribution different from the target policy. Their feedback can make value estimates diverge even when each ingredient seems reasonable alone. [1](https://incompleteideas.net/book/the-book-2nd.html)

DQN samples replayed transitions to reduce temporal correlation and improve reuse, and computes targets with a slowly updated/frozen target network:

$$y=r+\gamma\max_{a'}Q_{target}(s',a').$$

This slows the moving-target feedback but does not provide a universal convergence guarantee for nonlinear networks. Replay can contain stale or poorly covered data; max operators can cause overestimation. Monitor TD errors, value scales, coverage, and evaluation return. Double-Q ideas, target update schedules, and suitable exploration address additional failure modes rather than replacing sound environment design.
